faqs.q: What is a Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF (type QOF) used for?
faqs.a: Grade 100 four-leg chain sling made up with an oblong master link assembly at the top and a foundry hook on each of the four legs. A foundry hook has a wide, open throat with no latch, made for trunnions, ladle bails and handles too thick for a sling hook. With no latch, keep the load seated in the bowl of the hook.

faqs.q: What does the code QOF mean on Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF?
faqs.a: Chain sling make-ups are named by a letter code read from the top down: Q = quad leg; O = oblong master link; F = foundry hook. So a QOF sling is a quad leg sling with an oblong master link assembly at the top and a foundry hook on each of its four legs. The part numbers in the size table start IH-LR-CS-G100QOF and add the chain size, for example IH-LR-CS-G100QOF-6MM for 6 mm.

faqs.q: Which chain sizes does Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF come in?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF comes in 11 chain sizes, 6 mm to 26 mm chain, each with its own Indus part number from IH-LR-CS-G100QOF-6MM to IH-LR-CS-G100QOF-26MM. The chain and every fitting are matched in size and grade, so the chain size you pick sets the working load limit.

faqs.q: How do I specify the reach when ordering Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF?
faqs.a: For Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF, with oblong master link with sub-links at the top and a foundry hook on each leg, slings are made up to length. Quote the Indus part number for the chain size and the reach you need, measured from the bearing point of the top fitting to the bearing point of the hook, or send the load, the number of lifting points and the headroom and we will size the sling for you.

faqs.q: What is the working load limit of Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF is rated 3 to 56 t, legs up to 45° from vertical, depending on chain size, at a 4:1 design factor. On 16 mm chain the WLL is 21.2 t with each leg up to 45° from vertical and 15 t between 45° and 60°; on 26 mm chain it is 56 t and 40 t.

faqs.q: Why does Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF show two working load limits for each size?
faqs.a: The rating of a multi-leg sling depends on how far the legs spread. The table heads its columns by the angle between opposite legs: "up to 90°" means each leg is no more than 45° from vertical, and "90–120°" means each leg is between 45° and 60° from vertical. A chain sling is never used with its legs more than 60° from vertical. This applies to the oblong master link with sub-links at the top and a foundry hook on each leg on Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF.

faqs.q: What identification and test certificate come with Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF?
faqs.a: Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF carries a permanent tag and ships with a certificate. Each sling carries a permanent tag with its serial number, chain size, grade, reach and working load limit, and ships with the manufacturer's test certificate. The rating on the tag and certificate is the one that governs the sling in service. For third-party certification or a witnessed proof test, say so on the RFQ.

faqs.q: Can I swap a hook or link on Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF for one from another sling?
faqs.a: Only with a part of the same grade and size, because a sling is rated on its weakest component and a lower-grade hook or link pulls the whole sling down to that part's rating. Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF is built from Grade 100 alloy steel chain and fittings, so repairs and replacements should be Grade 100 parts as well; ask us for the matching fitting.

faqs.q: How should Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF be inspected and kept in service?
faqs.a: Before each lift the user looks over Grade 100 Four-Leg Chain Sling with Foundry Hooks, Type QOF for stretched or nicked chain, bent links and a deformed hook throat. A damaged sling is taken out of service, and it also needs periodic inspection by a competent person. The [Chain sling capacity chart: Grade 80 and Grade 100 WLL by legs and angle](/blog/chain-sling-capacity-chart) explains how working load, proof load and breaking load relate.

faqs.q: What is a Grade 100 Two-Leg Chain Sling with Grab Hooks, Type DOG (type DOG) used for?
faqs.a: Grade 100 two-leg chain sling made up with an oblong master link at the top and a grab hook on each of the two legs. A grab hook has a narrow throat that seats across a single chain link, so a leg can be hooked back onto its own chain to shorten it or to wrap the load.

faqs.q: What does the code DOG mean on Grade 100 Two-Leg Chain Sling with Grab Hooks, Type DOG?

So a DOG sling is a double leg sling with an oblong master link at the top and a grab hook on each of its two legs. The part numbers in the size table start IH-LR-CS-G100DOG and add the chain size, for example IH-LR-CS-G100DOG-6MM for 6 mm.

faqs.q: What is the working load limit of Grade 100 Two-Leg Chain Sling with Grab Hooks, Type DOG?

faqs.q: Why does Grade 100 Two-Leg Chain Sling with Grab Hooks, Type DOG show two working load limits for each size?
